scope_note: agent 0, sandbox 0, evaluation environment 0. The 2 containment hits are door interlocks; 3 of the 4 egress hits are electromagnetic emanation. Neither term is used in the AI-containment sense.

instrument: GPAI Code of Practice, Safety & Security chapter
scope_note: tool call 0, logs 0, telemetry 0, agent 1, logging 1 (an optional and/or list), sandbox 1 and isolation 1 - all in the same sentence, Appendix 4.4, under Insider Threats, as a sub-point of reducing the risk of model self-exfiltration. All four evaluation environment hits concern external validity, never security; all eleven contain hits are the verb.

Counted across all 247 control specifications: day 0, cadence 0, real-time 0, latency 0, delay 0. Time terms appear only as audit cadence (CEK-09, DCS-15, SEF-04, TVM-12, LOG-05). The only control explicitly about time is LOG-06 Clock Synchronization, whose purpose is to make timestamps comparable. 'withstand adversarial attempts' appears in the AIS-13 auditing guideline, not in the normative text, and without a measure.

instrument: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, AU-9 and enhancements
scope_note: Protects the integrity of records after creation, not their truth at creation. No term count for this control family in the evidence base.

instrument: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SC-7 Boundary Protection
object_protected: system boundary: deny-by-default, prevent exfiltration, dynamic isolation, fail secure, isolation of system components, restrict outgoing traffic, host-based protection
scope_note: Counted across the whole SC-7 family: period 0, frequency 0, time 0, delay 0, interval 0, day 0. The single `duration` occurrence is in SC-7.4 External Telecommunications Services: 'Document each exception to the traffic flow policy with a supporting mission or business need and duration of that need.' That duration is the lifetime of an administrative exception to the policy, not the endurance of a boundary under attack - so the one duration in the most comprehensive boundary-protection catalogue in existence measures paperwork, not endurance. SC-7.10 leaves the exfiltration-test frequency as an organization-defined parameter: an empty slot, which is where this project's clause lands.

instrument: Fujitsu: AI Sandboxes - A Threat Model, Taxonomy, and Measurement Framework
scope_note: The closest measurement framework in existence, and its containment dimension carries no time axis. The evidence base states this qualitatively; it gives no per-term counts for this instrument.

object_protected: six practices, all detection and reaction

scope_note: Read: introduction and cyber thresholds. Fully term-searched.

object_protected: customer-facing safety documentation for a Critical-candidate model
scope_note: 185,000 characters published for a model at a Critical capability threshold, with no containment hold time anywhere in it. Read: monitorability and infrastructure sections. Fully term-searched.
The single containment hit is generic. The single egress hit concerns bandwidth controls against exfiltration of multi-terabyte model weights - the object is the weights, not the agent.

instrument: Moon and Varshney: Containment Verification - AI Safety Guarantees Independent of Alignment
object_protected: the agentic framework (containment layer) rather than the model
scope_note: Deductive verification of boundary-event safety for every typed action the AI can emit, independent of capability, training and strategy. Instantiated on PocketFlow under havoc-oracle semantics. States the goal 'independent of alignment' in almost the same words as this project - and still has no time axis. Binary and static: it proves WHETHER a boundary holds under modelled assumptions, never HOW LONG it holds against an attacker who finds an unmodelled path.

instrument: Hossain et al.: The Containment Gap - How Deployed Agentic AI Frameworks Fail Public-Facing Safety Requirements
object_protected: six containment principles from a compositional model of agentic architectures
scope_note: Audits LangChain, AutoGPT and the OpenAI Agents SDK; none satisfies the principles natively, and memory integrity is missing from all three. Empirically validated against a memory-poisoning attack. Binary and static.

instrument: Metere: Methods for Formal Verification of Agent Skills - Three Layers Toward a Mechanically Checkable Capability-Containment Proof
object_protected: capability containment, mapped to EU AI Act Art. 9/13/15/16, NIS2, NIST AI RMF, FedRAMP/SP 800-53 (AC, AU, SI, SR, RA, PT), ISO/IEC 42001 and 23894
scope_note: Carries 'Capability-Containment Proof' in its title and has no hold time. Its only P > hit is a probability: it distinguishes statistical lower bounds from formal containment proofs, noting that the former lower P[dangerous output] while P > 0 survives at any non-trivial scale. This is exactly the misreading the P_wall / P_exp writing rule exists to prevent.
Cannot represent persistence by re-infection over ephemeral compute: there is no cron, no service and no on-disk implant to map (K-5). Assessment from SecureLayer7; no term count performed.

instrument: EU AI Act and NIST AI RMF, as mapped by CSA AICM
scope_note: Carried as one row because the evidence base treats them as one. CSA's own formal declarations: AIS-11 against the EU AI Act is No Mapping / Full Gap, with the addendum 'Include security boundaries for agents, for both AI System and AI Model, in Article 3'; against NIST AI RMF + 600-1 also Full Gap. AIS-13 against the EU AI Act is Full Gap - 'The EU AI Act does not provide requirements related to AIS-13' - and Full Gap against NIST. AIS-14 against the EU AI Act is Full Gap. This is a standards body's formal finding, not this project's assertion.

instrument: METR documented-incident catalogue (companion to the Frontier Risk Report)
object_protected: agent behaviour, scored for scope violation and concealment
scope_note: The most extensive public catalogue of AI agent incidents scores two axes, neither of which is duration. No entry records how long a control held. The two axes are overreach (how far beyond intended scope the agent knowingly went) and deception (steps taken to avoid detection or conceal actions). Downloadable as incidents.json; grading was done by Claude Opus 4.7.

counted=11; qualitative=6. 11 instruments where the absence of a time axis for containment was established by term count (5 full_text_term_count, 3 full_text_term_count_aggregated_over_cluster, 2 partial_read_full_term_search, 1 term_search_only), and 6 more by qualitative reading of the evidence base. Headline sentences use 11, because that is the number a reviewer can re-run; all 17 rows stay in the data. The figures of ten, twelve and fourteen instruments that appear in the evidence base are stale - they date from earlier drafts and were never reconciled.
